source_text:
Φράσας (Ὠριγένης)

ἀποφήνασθαι τὸν Κύριον, ὡς «οἱ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τευξόμενοι ἔσονται τότε ὡς ἄγγελοι,» ἔνθα πειράζουσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι, ἐπέφερεν· «Οἱ δὲ ἄγγελοι ἐκτὸς
ὄντες σαρκὸς ἐν μακαριότητος ἀκρότητι, διὰ τοῦτο καὶ δόξης εἰσί· καὶ ἡμᾶς δὲ ἄρα
ἐξισάζεσθαι μέλλοντας ἀγγέλοις ἀνάγκη δὴ σαρκῶν ὡσαύτως ἐκείνοις γυμνοὺς
ἔσεσθαι δεῖν.»
thought_title: The resurrected will be fleshless like angels
orientation: Origen, as reported by Methodius, is explaining Jesus' saying to the Sadducees that those who attain the resurrection will be like angels, and drawing the conclusion that they must therefore be without flesh.
pass_a_gloss: Origen having declared that the Lord pronounced, as "those who will attain the resurrection will then be equal to angels," where the Sadducees test him, he added: "But the angels, being outside of flesh in the height of blessedness, for this reason also are of glory; and we then, who are going to be made equal to angels, must necessarily be without flesh just as those ones."

choices.why: Literal rendering of the prepositional phrase with the participle, preserving the spatial sense of being apart from flesh rather than merely lacking it.
Literal rendering of the genitive of quality with the noun 'height,' matching the source's abstract spatial metaphor.
The infinitive δεῖν with the future infinitive conveys necessity; 'naked' preserves the literal sense of γυμνοὺς as stripped of flesh.

choices.english: who are going to be made equal to angels
choices.why: The participle with μέλλοντας conveys future intention; the passive infinitive of ἐξισάζω is rendered as 'to be made equal,' preserving the passive voice.
rejected: who will be equal to angels
who are about to become equal to angels

pass_b_english: Origen declared that the Lord pronounced, at the point where the Sadducees test him, that "those who attain the resurrection will then be equal to angels."

Origen then added: "The angels exist without flesh in the height of blessedness, and for this reason they also possess glory. And since we too are going to be made equal to angels, it must necessarily be that we will be without flesh just as they are."

problems.quote: he added: "The angels exist outside of flesh"
problems.why: Origen speaks, but quotation marks and 'he added' blur author vs. opponent

problems.quote: those who attain the resurrection will then be like angels
problems.why: Jesus says 'like angels' in heaven, not 'at the resurrection' specifically; Origen conflates timing
problems.fix: Note: Scripture says 'in heaven' not 'at resurrection'; author disputes Origen's gloss

problems.quote: Origen declared that when the Lord pronounced
problems.why: Unclear if Origen is being quoted or paraphrased; the quote that follows may be Origen's own words or Scripture.
problems.fix: Clarify whether the quoted material is Origen's commentary or Christ's words.

edits.old: Origen declared that when the Lord pronounced that those who attain the resurrection will then be like angels, at the point where the Sadducees test him, he added: "The angels exist outside of flesh in the height of blessedness, and for this reason they also possess glory. And since we too are going to be made equal to angels, it must necessarily be that we will be naked of flesh just as they are."
edits.new: Origen declared that the Lord pronounced, "Those who attain the resurrection will then be like angels," at the point where the Sadducees test him, and then Origen added: "The angels exist outside of flesh in the height of blessedness, and for this reason they also possess glory. And since we too are going to be made equal to angels, it must necessarily be that we will be naked of flesh just as they are."

fixed: The speaker attribution is now clarified: the first quotation is the Lord's words, and the second quotation is explicitly Origen's added commentary.
The Scripture quotation is now presented as Origen's report of the Lord's pronouncement, not as a direct citation of the Gospel text, so the timing issue is not introduced by the translation.
The distinction between the Lord's quoted words and Origen's added commentary is now clear.

problems.fix: Distinguish Jesus' words from Origen's commentary.

problems.why: The quotation marks end after 'angels' but Origen's continuation lacks clear boundary.
problems.fix: Use quotation marks for all of Origen's statement.

problems.why: Origen likely said 'naked' meaning 'without flesh' but this is author's pejorative framing.
problems.fix: Note: author polemically renders Origen's view.

problems.quote: those who attain the resurrection will then be like angels
problems.why: Luke 20:35-36 says 'equal to angels' (isangeloi), not 'like angels' (hos angeloi).
problems.fix: Use 'equal to' or note textual variant.

problems.why: Ambiguous whether Origen is being quoted approvingly or cited as an opponent to be refuted.
problems.fix: Clarify whether the work endorses or critiques Origen's position.

problems.why: Unusual phrasing; 'divested of flesh' or 'without flesh' would be clearer.

Speaker attribution: The English already uses quotation marks for all of Origen's statement, including his added commentary.

Wrong scripture: Changed 'like angels' to 'equal to angels' to match Luke 20:35-36 (isangeloi).
Speaker attribution: The English already presents Origen as the speaker of the added commentary, which is sufficient for the fragment's framing.
Mistranslation 'naked of flesh': Changed to 'without flesh' for clarity.

last_rejected.quote: those who attain the resurrection will then be equal to angels
last_rejected.source_quote: οἱ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τευξόμενοι ἔσονται τότε ὡς ἄγγελοι
last_rejected.why: The Lord is quoted as saying they will be as angels (ὡς). Equality (ἐξισάζεσθαι) is Origen's next inference, not the saying.
last_rejected.fix: those who attain the resurrection will then be as angels.
last_rejected.ruling: Source οἱ ... ἔσονται τότε ὡς ἄγγελοι means 'will be like/as angels'; 'equal to angels' overstates ὡς, but ἐξισάζεσθαι immediately follows and the sense is close. Minor.
